- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational

- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced

- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.

- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum

- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Karen Reiner, Coordinator

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.

- Washington St., Alexandria, VA 22314 or phone: 800- 708-7581. PA programs and
- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- Integrative Studies
- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum
- Special Approval: Program director permission required.
- ITGS 490 - Portfolio Seminar
- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology
- Karen Reiner, Coordinator
- 269-471-3622
- Halenz Hall (Science Complex)
- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Preference is given to applicants who have a broad academic background with a
- baccalaureate degree. The minimum entrance requirement is 96 semester credits

- The prerequisites for admission to the MOT program are listed
- below. Prerequisites must be taken from regionally accredited colleges or

- Karen Reiner, 269-471-3622 (Haughey Hall 217)
- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.
- The National Directory of PA Programs may be ordered from APAP at 950 N.
- Washington St., Alexandria, VA 22314 or phone: 800- 708-7581. PA programs and
- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum
- Special Approval: Program director permission required.
- ITGS 490 - Portfolio Seminar
- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- overall. The Dental Aptitude Test (DAT) must be taken not later than October of

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.

- Washington St., Alexandria, VA 22314 or phone: 800- 708-7581. PA programs and
- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum

- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.
- The National Directory of PA Programs may be ordered from APAP at 950 N.
- Washington St., Alexandria, VA 22314 or phone: 800- 708-7581. PA programs and
- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum
- Special Approval: Program director permission required.

- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.

- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- Integrative Studies
- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum
- Special Approval: Program director permission required.
- ITGS 490 - Portfolio Seminar
- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.

- Physician assistants (PAs), members of a health-care team, practice medicine with
- supervision of licensed physicians. PAs perform a wide range of medical duties
- from basic primary care to high-technology specialty procedures. Professional PA
- education offered at any one of more than 100 accredited schools is an intensive
- 2–3 year program. Most PA programs are moving toward requiring a bachelors
- degree including courses in biology, chemistry, English, humanities/social science,
- mathematics, and psychology. The level of the science courses varies from
- program to program; consequently, each school should be consulted about its
- prerequisite requirements. Acceptance to a professional program typically requires
- an extensive health-care experience such as nurse assistant, medical/X-ray lab
- technician, respiratory therapist, paramedic, hospital aide, and emergency medical
- technician.
- The National Directory of PA Programs may be ordered from APAP at 950 N.
- Washington St., Alexandria, VA 22314 or phone: 800- 708-7581. PA programs and
- education can be accessed via the web: www.aapa.org.

- ITGS 290 - Becoming Integrative
- Credits: 3
- This class is the first component of the Integrative Studies core. It introduces the
- core knowledge, skills, and values for interdisciplinary work in academic and work
- settings. Students learn the developmental process of integrative studies, the
- fundamentals of interdisciplinary research, and the integration of personal,
- educational, and professional goals in preparation for their chosen vocational
- path.
- Grade Mode: Normal (A-F,I,W)
- Recommended: BS Integrative Studies majors are advised to complete this class in
- their first semester.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online
- Year Offering: Annually
- Term Offering: Fall, Spring, Summer
- College Code: CEIS
- ITGS 310 - Integrative Skills
- In this core course, integrative studies majors build critical thinking about
- interdisciplinary real-world contexts. After surveying research methods across
- disciplines, students explore approaches to integrative research and craft their
- own small research projects.
- Schedule Type: Interactive Online, Self-Paced
- ITGS 390 - Integrative Fieldwork
- This course provides students with the opportunity to learn and apply integrative
- skills through 100 or more hours of supervised work or research. Students also
- participate in class discussions reflecting on their field experiences. It is
- recommended that students meet with the instructor the semester beforehand to
- discuss class requirements and placement options.
- Grade Mode: Satisfactory (S,U,I,W)
- Prerequisite(s): ITGT 290. Open to undergraduate students admitted to online
- degree completion programs.
- Schedule Type: Practicum
- Special Approval: Program director permission required.

- This class provides students an opportunity to weave together their education,
- skills, abilities, and professional career experience to create one cohesive narrative
- in an integrated portfolio. Students will showcase their digital portfolios in a video
- presentation.
- Schedule Type: Seminar

- Cytotechnology is a specialty within a broad field of clinical laboratory science.
- Cytotechnologists aid in the early detection of disease by differentiating normal,
- atypical, and malignant cells. In recognizing microscopic abnormalities of cells and
- cellular patterns from the various body sites, the cytotechnologist assists the
- pathologist in detecting cancer at its earliest and potentially most curable stage.
- Medical applications of cytologic techniques are constantly expanding, particularly
- in the diagnosis and
- management of the cancer patient.
- Students pursuing a career in cytotechnology should complete the first two or
- three years (according to their selection of school for technical education) and
- then complete the professional courses offered at Loma Linda University or
- another school. For
- more information: www.ascp.org.
